In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two stocks of Sprague-Dawleys differ in baseline performance on DRL 72 and in the pharmacological profile of several compounds on DRL 73.

the Holtzman rat is a more sensitive animal model for antidepressant screening and 5-HT receptor agonist screening than the Harlan Sprague Dawley rat, but not for the amphetamine-induced disruption of DRL 72 performance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DRL 22-sec and DRL 72 sec schedules of reinforcement may not be sensitive to the same pharmacological treatments in all rat stocks.
the Holtzman rats were more sensitive to the behavioral and hypothermic effects of the 5-HT agonists, imipramin and ketanserin, than were Harlan rats.
the Harlan rat stock is more sensitive to drugs that primarily act on the serotonergic system, while the Holtzman rat stock appears to be more sensitive to drugs acting upon the dopaminergic system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DRL 76-sec behavioral screen is sensitive enough to detect pharmacological effects in two different stocks of rats.
the Harlan rat is a more appropriate animal model for studying the pharmacological effects of 5-HT compounds.
the Holtzman Sprague Dawley rat is not a suitable substitute for the Harlan Sprague Dawley rats in the DRL 78-sec behavioral test.
